tsbs.title: 3VZ-E V6 head gasket — Special Service Campaign V06
tsbs.summary: Head gasket replacement for 3VZ-E trucks built 1/90–10/94; replaced a 1996 policy adjustment and expired 24 September 2018.

timeline.change: All-new steel body on the Hilux frame; coil-sprung four-link rear axle; 22R-E or 3VZ-E; rear-wheel ABS standard on SR5 V6
V6 trucks built 1/90–10/94: Toyota said its 3VZ-E head-gasket failures were primarily limited to this production window (campaign V06, expired 2018). Ask for proof of the gasket job
Facelift: one-piece front bumper, modular headlamps, new interior trim; US two-door sales end August 1992
Two-door production ends May 1993; Japan's Hilux Surf gains the 1KZ-TE 3.0 turbo-diesel (August)
Side-impact door beams added for the US
Final year; keeps door beams. V6 trucks built after October 1994 fall outside the V06 campaign window. Replaced by the Prado-based 1996 4Runner

identify.intro: The 2nd gen shares its nose, front suspension and engines with the 1989–95 Hilux, and rare two-doors and Japanese Surfs muddy the water.

items.head: Two-door
items.body: Built from launch to May 1993 (US sales ended August 1992, Canada through 1993). Toyota priced them above the four-door because of the chicken tax, so they are genuinely rare.

items.head: Pre- or post-facelift
items.body: 1990–91 trucks have rectangular sealed-beam headlamps; the 1992-on facelift brought one-piece bumpers and modular headlamps.

items.head: Engine and transfer case
items.body: V6 (3VZ-E) trucks got a chain-driven transfer case; four-cylinder (22R-E) trucks kept the older gear-driven case.

items.head: Model codes
items.body: Toyota coded V6 trucks VZN130 and diesel trucks LN130/KZN130; the diesel, wide-body and limited-slip versions were Japanese or European, not US-market 4Runners.

values.intro: Still the cheapest way into an old 4Runner, but clean V6 five-speed SR5s now pull well above the pack.
values.note: Based on 22 Bring a Trailer sales from May to October 2026 (median about $11,750). The top sale was a 1993 SR5 V6 five-speed at $36,250.

paragraphs: Japan's Hilux Surf (N120/N130) came with diesels the US never got: the 2L-TE, 3L and, from August 1993, the 3.0 1KZ-TE turbo-diesel, plus wide-body trims. All are now older than 25 years, so they can be imported without meeting US federal safety standards, but they are right-hand drive and state titling and emissions rules still apply.

production.intro: Built at Tahara, Japan (and by a joint venture in China), from 1989 to August 1995.

items.k: US sales (calendar year; 1989 sales are listed on the 1st gen, 1995 includes early 3rd gens)

maintenance.description: Toyota 4Runner second generation (1990–1995) maintenance schedule from Toyota's 1993 Pickup and 4Runner repair manual: oil every 7,500 mi or 12 months (3,750 under Schedule A), plugs and air filter every 30,000, coolant first at 45,000 then every 30,000, gear oils every 15,000 under Schedule A.
maintenance.intro: Toyota's maintenance chapter for the 1993 Pickup and 4Runner (22R-E four and 3VZ-E V6) has two schedules. Schedule A is for towing or campers, short trips below freezing, long idling, and dusty, rough, muddy or salted roads. Schedule B is for everything else. A 4Runner that goes off-road belongs on Schedule A. Toyota says to keep repeating the same intervals after 60,000 miles.
maintenance.schedule_note: From Toyota's 1993 Pickup and 4Runner repair manual, maintenance schedule (Schedule B shown). The 1990–1995 trucks share engines; check your own book for your year.

items: Inspect steering linkage, ball joints and dust covers, drive shaft boots
Inspect transmission, transfer case and differential oil levels
Check the steering gear box for leaks
Inspect brake linings, pads and lines
Check chassis and body bolts; check idle speed after the first 7,500
Replace the air filter and spark plugs
Repack front wheel bearings and thrust bush grease, 4WD (36 months; 48 for 2WD)
Engine coolant, first replacement; then every 30,000 mi / 24 months
Replace the fuel tank cap gasket (72 months)
Inspect drive belts (first at 30,000 / 36 months, then 60,000; after that every 7,500 mi / 12 months)

maintenance.severe: Toyota's Schedule A: engine oil and filter every 3,750 miles or 6 months; inspect the air filter every 3,750 miles on dusty roads and replace it every 30,000; change the automatic or manual transmission, transfer case and differential oil every 15,000 miles or 24 months; grease the propeller shafts every 7,500 miles or 12 months; inspect brakes, steering linkage, ball joints and drive shaft boots every 7,500. On the 3VZ-E V6, Schedule A replaces the timing belt at 60,000 miles for trucks used with long idling or low-speed driving. Toyota says to re-grease the propeller shaft daily if it has been under water.

age_items.why: Toyota: if the propeller shaft has been immersed, re-grease it daily.

age_items.when: Every 2 years after the first change
age_items.why: Toyota's interval after the first change is 30,000 miles or 24 months.
Toyota moves the belt inspection to every 7,500 miles or 12 months after the second period.
